corrections.source_says: Add the promising and trivial idea outcomes from the same cohort comparison. Promising: 2023 count 17, mean 0.85 (SD 0.93); 2024 count 11, mean 0.50 (SD 1.06); cohort F(1, 39) = 2.504, p = 0.122 controlling for total ideas, and F(1, 39) = 4.5, p = 0.041 after also including Minecraft experience. The narrative describes the adjusted promising-idea effect as favoring 2024 despite its lower unadjusted mean; adjusted means and signed coefficients are not reported. Trivial: 2023 count 24, mean 1.20 (SD 1.36); 2024 count 38, mean 1.73 (SD 2.53); cohort F(1, 39) = 0.019, p = 0.891 controlling for total ideas, and F(1, 39) = 0.011, p = 0.917 after also including Minecraft experience. These are counts of ideas per student, with cohort sample sizes 20 and 22, not additional participants.

confirmed: Read the complete 46,948-character markdown and all 15 PDF pages, including the references; no appendix or supplementary material is described. The PDF running header says 2025, in press, The Social Innovations Journal, consistent with the form's author-manuscript version; retrieval.json identifies the OSF revised submission file (PDF p. 1 and running headers; pp. 13?15, References).

The paper contains one non-randomized cohort comparison: 2023 without JeepyTA and 2024 with access to JeepyTA. quasi_people and observational context are correct, and there is no qualifying randomized people study (PDF p. 2, Study Purpose; p. 4, Application of JeepyTA and Methods; pp. 11?12, Discussion).

The analyzed cohort sizes are 20 and 22 students, represented by 42 play journals, below the 50-person threshold. The form correctly leaves randomized counts null; no randomized sample or exclusion count is reported (PDF p. 4, Data Source; p. 7, Coding the data and Data Analysis).

JeepyTA used GPT-3.5, specifically gpt-3.5-turbo-16k-0613, in the course discussion forum; students proposed educational applications of Minecraft and were encouraged to thought-partner with the tool (PDF pp. 3?4, Application of JeepyTA).

The outcomes were coded on student-produced journal sections rather than self-reported creativity; fully formed ideas were defined by detail and concrete examples, supporting elaboration and criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output = met (PDF pp. 4?5, Coding the data and Table 1; p. 7, coding procedure).

S1-O1 reported numbers match: 2023 N=20, 7 fully formed ideas, mean 0.35 (SD 0.49); 2024 N=22, 18 fully formed ideas, mean 0.82 (SD 0.96). Cohort F(1, 39) = 4.652, p = 0.037 with total ideas controlled, and F(1, 39) = 4.83, p = 0.034 with Minecraft experience also included, exactly as the manuscript prints them (PDF p. 8, Tables 2?3; p. 9, Fully Formed Ideas).

S1-O2 reported numbers match: 48 total ideas, mean 2.40 (SD 1.43), in 2023; 67 total ideas, mean 3.05 (SD 2.3), in 2024. No test of the cohort difference in total ideas is reported; total ideas is an ANCOVA covariate (PDF p. 7, Data Analysis; pp. 8?10, RQ1 and Tables 2?3).

S1-O3 counts match Table 4: JeepyTA-driven ideas total 50 from 18 students, comprising 36 trivial, 8 promising, and 6 fully formed; student-driven ideas total 17 from 10 students, comprising 2 trivial, 3 promising, and 12 fully formed. These are overlapping subsets of the 2024 cohort, not an additional sample (PDF p. 10, Table 4 and explanatory paragraph).

S1-O3 theme frequencies match: teamwork/collaboration in 10 students' responses, creativity with storytelling in 8, and virtual field trips in 6; student-driven architecture in 3 and math in 2. This is descriptive within-2024 evidence, with no 2023 homogeneity comparison or statistical test reported (PDF p. 11, RQ3 continuation and Homogeneity of ideas).

The form correctly flags the manuscript's internal discrepancy: student-driven trivial ideas are 2 in Table 4 and its p. 10 narrative, but 5 in the p. 11 Homogeneity of ideas paragraph. This is a source inconsistency, not a numerical transcription error in the form (PDF pp. 10?11).

The one-line finding's numerical content and descriptive homogeneity statement are supported; the citation for its degrees of freedom needs the additional p. 9 locator noted above (PDF pp. 8?11, Tables 2?4 and RQ1/RQ3).
This is an original cohort analysis, not a synthesis; the empty pooled-estimate fields and null synthesis counts are appropriate (PDF pp. 4?11, Methods and Results).
summary: The manuscript reports a non-randomized cohort comparison of 42 students, so the observational classification and exclusion from the core are correct. The recorded numbers match the PDF, but the form omits promising/trivial outcomes and sample overlap, misses an Elsevier affiliation, and needs corrections to outcome metadata and one citation.
